(B)The graph will still show a linear relationship that extrapolates to the origin, but with a larger slope.
(C)The graph will still show a linear relationship, but it will not extrapolate to the origin.
(D)The graph will not show a linear relationship, but it will still extrapolate to the origin.
Which of the following statement is NOT a correct assumption of the classical model of an ideal gas?
(A)The molecules are in random motion
(B)The volume of the molecules is negligible compared with the volume occupied by the gas.
(C)The molecules obey Newton’s laws of motion.
(D)The collisions between molecules are inelastic.
(E)The only appreciable forces on the molecules are those that occur during collisions.
An ideal gas is initially in state 1 at a temperature of 200 K. The gas is taken through the two reversible
thermodynamic processes shown in the PV diagram above. The process from state 1 to state 2 is isothermal. The
process from state 2 to state 3 is isobaric. What is the temperature of the gas when it is in state 3?
